statement.text: If $\omega(n)$ counts the number of distinct prime factors of $n$, then is it true that, for every $k\geq 1$, $ \liminf_{n\to \infty}\sum_{0\leq i<k}\omega(n+i)\leq k+\pi(k)? $ Is it true that $ \limsup_{n\to \infty}\left(\sum_{0\leq i<k}\omega(n+i)\right) \frac{\log\log n}{\log n}=1? $

title: Erdős Problem #890
